choices.why: The compound ἀξιάγαστος conveys value beyond estimation; 'inestimable' is literal but 'beyond price' better captures the theological weight in context.
The verb καθιστὰς requires a result; 'made evident' reflects the causative sense better than a bare adjective.
Imperfect tense indicates ongoing action in past context; 'was bringing forward' is literal but 'was presenting' fits the rhetorical display of love.
Perfect middle indicative conveys completed action with present result; 'we have been freed' captures this better than 'we were freed'.
Subjunctive after purpose clause ἵνα; 'might abolish' reflects the intended effect better than 'might render idle' in this theological context.
Perfect participle emphasizes completed state of loss; 'utterly lost' conveys the totality better than 'lost' or 'undone'.

pass_b_english: Our Lord Jesus Christ has made plain the Father’s love beyond price, showing it to us in the completion of the fleshly dispensation and in the suffering of the cross, even as he declared, 'For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.' (John 3:16)
He truly gave his own Son for our sake.

We have been redeemed; we have been freed from death and sin. The Word became flesh and dwelt in us not for any other reason, but so that, having endured the death of the flesh, he might triumph over every ruler and authority and abolish the one who holds the power of death— that is, the devil— and thus destroy corruption and put away the sin that tyrannizes over us.

In this way he declares inactive henceforth that ancient curse which human nature endured in Adam, as the firstfruit of the race and as the root of the first, for Adam, having transgressed the commandment, became guilty before his Maker and thereby became both accursed and held fast by death.
Yet the Lord of all again brought destruction upon those utterly lost.
For the Son came down from heaven, taking away sins, justifying the ungodly through faith, transforming human nature into incorruption as God, and bringing it back to the beginning.

Our Lord Jesus Christ truly demonstrated the Father's love toward us, making it evident through the end of the fleshly economy and the passion on the cross, saying, 'For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.' (John 3:16)
